nakhāsikhāsutta:
[Nakhasikhā+sutta]  CL=7 (1)
When the Lord Buddha was residing at the Jetavana Monastery in Sāvatthi, he placed a small amount of sand on his fingernail and said, 'The suffering that remains for a sotāpanna (stream-enterer) is as insignificant as the sand on this nail, whereas the suffering that has been eradicated is as vast as the earth. (2)
The discourse illustrates the contrast between beings who pass away and are reborn in the human realm versus those who are reborn in other realms (such as hell, the animal realm, etc.). The number of beings reborn in the human realm is as minuscule as the sand on the Buddha"s nail, while the number of beings reborn in other realms is as vast as the earth. (3)
The discourse further explains the impermanent and unstable nature of form (rupa), sensation (vedanā), perception (saññā), mental formations (saṅkhāra), and consciousness (viññāṇa). Their firmness or unchanging nature is so insubstantial that it is likened to the sand on the Buddha"s nail. Practicing the noble path that leads to the cessation of suffering is subtle and not easily discerned, yet it is the path to liberation.
